title: Compact launch keeper checklist & locality timetable (Feb 2025) - sketch
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-facing checklist + locality-aware timetable for small/medium launches where we need a quick but auditable canary followed by staggered regional ramp. Aim: safe fast path when risk is low but we still want guardrails (latency, error-rate, cost).

TL;DR:
- 4-hour launch window per region (default) with 15/30/60/120 minute ramp steps.
- Locality-first routing applied: start in low-traffic region(s) closest to target customer cohort.
- Prefix cache priming and KV warmup run 45m before first traffic shift.
- Canary traffic target: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% -> 25% -> full (subject to SLOs).

Quick checklist (operator pocket cards) - to be checked live (checkboxes for shift lead):
- [ ] Preflight telemetry snapshot (baseline 24h): latency P50/P95, errors, token burn - link to dashboard
- [ ] Smoke tests green (unit smoke + e2e smoke): smoke-suite/compact-launch-2025
- [ ] Canary model pinned version verified in config and routing table (model: rwd-220b-v3-q4)
- [ ] Config commit tag exists and is referenced in release notes (git tag + PR)
- [ ] KMS/HSM key access validated for private-deploy customers in the window
- [ ] Observability alerts set for latency delta + error spike + throughput anomaly (templates: latency-regen, token-bleed)
- [ ] Rollback runbook open and assigned (who toggles the route / who executes gateway rollback)
- [ ] Communication channel set: #release-ops + incident bridge owner assigned
- [ ] Canaries provisioned on dedicated pool (if required) or verified fallback target ready

Locality timetable (operator-facing) - sample 4 hour per-region flow (times relative to T0 = first traffic shift):
- T0 -45m: KV cache & prefix priming job (run twice if model variant changed). Command: "tools/prime-prefix --model rwd-220b-v3-q4 --dry-run=false --threads=8"
- T0 -15m: Final telemetry snapshot + open watchlist doc. Confirm all smoke checks green.
- T0: shift 0.5% traffic (route rule: user_cohort=beta OR shard=42). Monitor first 5 full requests for quality regressions.
- T0 +15m: if stable (error < 0.5% delta, latency P95 < baseline +120ms) -> increase to 2%
- T0 +45m: increase to 5% unless throttled by cost gate or spike in errors
- T0 +1h45m: increase to 25% for region; observe 30m - 60m
- T0 +2h45m: decide full roll (regional full) or hold & escalate
- If full: regional full at T0 +3h; proceed to next region after 30m steady state

Decision gates and signals (explicit):
- Block to increase if any of:
  - sustained error-rate (5xx) > baseline +0.8% over 10m window
  - latency P95 > baseline +200ms over 5m window
  - sampling-based quality regression: automated evals on sampled responses show drop in BLEU/ROUGE or safety flags increase by >10%
- Soft warning: cost burn > expected projection by 30% -> pause and investigate; optional scale-down

Model variant fallback policy (compact):
- Primary: rwd-220b-v3-q4 (quantized)
- Fallback chain: rwd-220b-v3-q8 -> rwd-160b-v2-q4 -> hosted-guard-128b
- Routing: runtime config will attempt same-arch variant first; if N consecutive failures (N=5 per minute) then route to next variant with a short trial window (5m) before full switchover.

Prefix caching & KV warmup notes (uncommon in other docs):
- Why: first token latencies on long-tail prompts can spike and mislead SRE lead during canary.
- How: run a quick set of synthetic prefix sequences sampled from production logs (anonymized). Target 10k prefixes over 30m to warm the LRU caches on GPU nodes.
- Observe cache hit ratio increase; abort canary if hit ratio doesn’t reach threshold (>= 60%).

Release notes draft (compact format - operator to copy to product release page):
Title: 2025-02-?? Compact launch: rwd-220b-v3-q4
Summary: Small rollout of rwd-220b-v3 quantized runtime to improve latency and reduce token cost for inline chat features.
What changed:
- Deployed rwd-220b-v3-q4 with new kernel selection heuristics for short context workloads.
- Enabled prefix-caching priming job as part of launch flow.
- Updated runtime fallback chain and routing policy for locality-first canaries.
Impact:
- Expected latency improvement: ~15-25ms P50 for short prompts; P95 improvement depends on prefix warming.
- Cost: projected ~8% lower token cost on targeted cohorts.
Rollout plan:
- Canary in region-us-west-2 then stagger to eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 if stable.
Notes for customers:
- No user-visible changes expected; in case of anomalies, toggle back to previous model via console (route control -> model pin).
Linked tickets: JIRA-ENG-4821, JIRA-ENG-4876

Post-release quick retro template (to fill in within 48h):
- Actual timeline (T0 etc)
- Signals observed (latency P50/P95, error% trends, sampling quality notes)
- Was prefix warmup effective? (yes/no + numbers)
- Any rollback events and reason
- Follow-ups (owners + due dates)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Does prefix priming need to be scheduled earlier for ap-southeast-1 because of cold KV caches? (ask platform-eng)
- Confirm whether cost-monitoring alert should be add to automated gate (Lila to follow up)
- Should we add a lightweight A/B prompt-level eval for hallucination rate during canary? (Ethan scope)

Runbook snippets (for cut & paste into incident breadcrumb):
- To pause rollout: "endpointctl route set-weight --route <route> --weight 0 --note 'operator pause'"
- To fallback model manually: "runtimectl set-variant --endpoint <id> --variant rwd-220b-v3-q8 --ttl 300"
- To force prefix-prime: "tools/prime-prefix --model <model> --sample-id latest-prod-samples --force"

Slack signoffs (day of launch):
- Operator: @marisol (lead)
- Observability: @ethan (watcher)
- Platform escalation: @omar (on-call)
- Product comms: @lila (draft external note)

Notes to operator: keep watchlist window open in console and comment timestamps into this doc for the retro (makes post-mortem quicker).

End of sketch.

---
Change-log: 2025-02-10 initial sketch by Marisol; 2025-02-15 added prefix priming notes and model-fallback chain (Lila review)
